newsitem.title: FRANCE: French deputy urges weaker franc, govt reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: French deputy urges weaker franc, govt reshuffle.

text.p: A senior French parliamentarian from President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe's RPR party called on Tuesday for a government reshuffle and a weaker franc to help boost consumption.
Pierre Mazeaud, who is head of the National Assembly's legal committee, said in an interview with Radio Shalom that the reshuffle should be carried out at the beginning of 1997.

It was "necessary to envisage a ministerial reshuffle," and "necessary to modify" policies, Mazeaud said, adding that the "franc fort", or strong franc, policy followed in France over the last decade could not go on unchanged.
"The policy of the strong franc cannot continue in the manner it is right now," he said in the interview.
"I think we need in some way to relate our currency to our worth," he said. "We must also let the franc float a little. What is most important in the short term is a recovery of consumption."
